headline: Ipswich and Nott'm Forest share points despite a decisive xG gap

sentences.text: Ipswich Town and Nott'm Forest drew 1–1 in Premier League matchweek 8, but the scoreline concealed a substantial difference in chance production.
Nott'm Forest registered 17 shots to Ipswich's 7 and led expected goals 2.29 to 0.46, a gap of 1.83.
The visitors also had 5 shots on target against 3, created 2 big chances to Ipswich's 1 and won 5 corners while Ipswich had none.
Possession was almost even, with Nott'm Forest at 50.6% and Ipswich at 49.4%, so control of the ball did not reflect the difference in threat.
Nott'm Forest took the lead in the 13th minute through Neco Williams, assisted by Daniel Muñoz.
Ipswich levelled in the 41st minute when Julio Enciso scored, leaving the teams 1–1 at half-time.
Neither side scored after the break, despite Nott'm Forest's overall advantage in attempts and expected goals.
The recorded attempts excluding goals showed 2 saved and 4 off target for Ipswich, compared with 3 saved, 11 off target and 2 blocked for Nott'm Forest.
Ipswich came in with 6 points from their previous 5 league matches, while Nott'm Forest had taken 4 from their last 5.
Before kick-off Ipswich were 10th on 9 points and Nott'm Forest 19th on 5; afterwards Ipswich moved to 9th with 10 points and Nott'm Forest to 16th with 6.
The point therefore lifted both teams in the standings, although the table return was modest relative to the contrast in their attacking numbers.
Ipswich used a 4-2-3-1 and Nott'm Forest a 3-4-2-1, but the final score stayed level after the early exchange of goals.
